description:
`_strip_pk_constraints` in `benchbox/platforms/questdb.py` handles three
forms of PRIMARY KEY declaration.  The named-constraint form uses `\w+` to
match the constraint name:

  r",?\s*CONSTRAINT\s+\w+\s+PRIMARY\s+KEY\s*\([^)]*\)"

This will not match double-quoted constraint names like:
  CONSTRAINT "pk_lineitem" PRIMARY KEY (l_orderkey, l_linenumber)

TPC-H, TPC-DS, SSB, and all other benchmark schemas currently in BenchBox
use unquoted constraint names, so this is not a known active failure.  It is
a latent fragility that will bite silently if a new benchmark or a DDL
generator upgrade starts quoting identifiers.

Flagged during Phase 1 remediation review (2026-04-16) as a nit.

preserves.behavior: All five existing TestCreateSchemaBranches PK stripping tests continue to pass
_strip_fk_constraints is unchanged - only _strip_pk_constraints regex is modified

verifications.description: All PK stripping tests pass including new quoted-name test
verifications.expected: All tests pass (6 PK-related + existing tests)

work_units.notes:
In `benchbox/platforms/questdb.py`, `_strip_pk_constraints` (around line 694):

Change:
  r",?\s*CONSTRAINT\s+\w+\s+PRIMARY\s+KEY\s*\([^)]*\)"
To:
  r',?\s*CONSTRAINT\s+(?:"[^"]+"|`[^`]+`|\w+)\s+PRIMARY\s+KEY\s*\([^)]*\)'

The pattern accepts:
  - Double-quoted:   CONSTRAINT "pk_t" PRIMARY KEY (id)
  - Backtick-quoted: CONSTRAINT `pk_t` PRIMARY KEY (id)
  - Bare:            CONSTRAINT pk_t PRIMARY KEY (id)

Add one test in TestCreateSchemaBranches:

  def test_strip_pk_constraints_quoted_name(self, questdb_stubs):
      adapter = QuestDBAdapter()
      stmt = 'CREATE TABLE t (id INT, CONSTRAINT "pk_t" PRIMARY KEY (id))'
      result = adapter._strip_pk_constraints(stmt)
      assert "PRIMARY KEY" not in result.upper()
      assert "CONSTRAINT" not in result.upper()
      assert "id INT" in result

Run all existing _strip_pk_ tests to confirm no regressions.
work_units.summary: Extend named-constraint regex and add test
